agreements.statement: Both participants independently confirm H1: the S1 deployment to payment at 2026-08-16T19:59:39.582Z (before 0ac8e4a3..., after 84d38a2...) is the causal trigger for every-valid-charge failure.

Both localize the defect identically: validateCard at src/payment/card.js:12 contains an inverted/contradictory allowed-card-type check whose throw text 'cannot process' rejects a card that the trace marks card_valid=true, card_type=visa.
Both agree on the error-onset boundary: zero error-call span metric pre-deployment on a healthy backend vs. error metric value 1 exceeding the 0.2 threshold at ~8 calls/sec post-deployment.

Both reject the paymentUnreachable=true flag as the direct cause, on the same ground: the only erroring trace shows an internal card-validation rejection, not an unreachable/dependency error, so the flag is not on the observed failure path.
Both bound the blast radius to payment service, demo environment, version 84d38a2..., and characterize the outcome as critical every-valid-charge failure.

contradictions.statement: No material contradiction between participants. The only surface divergence - the log names 'mastercard' while the trace card_type is 'visa' - is treated identically by both as evidence of the mangled acceptance check rather than as competing root causes.

Minor terminological divergence only: P1 frames H2 as a reachability-style flag hypothesis, P2 frames the same as a connectivity/dependency hypothesis; both reject it consistently, so no analytic conflict.

blind_spots.statement: paymentUnreachable=true remains an unexplained residual observation. Both reject it as non-causal based on the trace, but neither explains why the flag is true, how it interacts with the deployed build, or verifies (by actually toggling it) that failures persist; both only propose the toggle as an untested test.

The exact nature of the inversion is asserted but not evidenced by a code-diff item in the revision; both label the condition 'inverted/reversed' without a before/after source diff item, so the precise failure branch is an inference rather than a pinned fact.

Both reject paymentFailure (95067a1e = 0) without testing the flag path; P1 mentions it only as an alternative and P2 folds it into the flag-rejection reasoning, leaving that hypothesis only lightly falsified.

Neither participant interrogates the 'charge driver stands in for storefront traffic' known limit or whether the 8 calls/sec rate and the single exemplar trace are representative of all callers - the 'every charge' claim rests on one exemplar.

unique_findings.statement: P1 proposes a deploy-before/rollback test (T2, revert to 0ac8e4a3...) to causally confirm S1 and a unit test of validateCard across VISA, MasterCard, and an unsupported type (T3), and explicitly enumerates the paymentFailure=0 flag toggle as a distinct alternative to falsify.

P2 explicitly surfaces and reasons about the mastercard/visa textual mismatch as a residual inconsistency, attributing it to message-vs-enforced-policy divergence of the deployed defect, and crisply states the non-causality argument that paymentUnreachable=true is 'not on the observed failure path'.
